candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Genesis
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis, Section XIV.18. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13, ed. J. Gwynn / Schaff (1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 360 AD)

Melchizedek brings forth bread and wine, blessing Abram. Ephrem treats Melchizedek as the supreme OT type of Christ — priest without genealogy, king of righteousness (melek-ṣedeq), king of peace (Salem = shalom). The bread-and-wine offering directly prefigures the Eucharist; the absence of bloody sacrifice makes Melchizedek's priesthood superior to the Aaronic. Tewahedo eucharistic theology preserves this typology load-bearingly: the Tewahedo Anaphora invokes Melchizedek explicitly as the priestly archetype that Christ fulfils, drawing on Heb 5-7 and Ephrem's exegetical lead.

candidates.source_name: Athanasius of Alexandria / Orationes contra Arianos II.13
candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos II.13 (c. 350 AD)

'And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was the priest of the most high God' — Athanasius marks the Melchizedek-priesthood as the PRE-INCARNATIONAL christophany / typological-shadow of the eternal-high-priesthood the Word exercises post-incarnation per Heb 7. The priest hiereus tou theou tou hypsistou (priest of God Most High) and the bread-and-wine offering both prefigure the Word's-Eucharistic-priesthood. Heb 7:3's 'without father, without mother, without descent' — Athanasius reads not of Melchizedek-the-man but of Melchizedek-the-type / the Word he prefigures: only the eternal-Son is literally without-descent (anepidektos genealogias). Tewahedo Anaphora liturgy preserves the Melchizedek-Christ priestly-typology at the bread-and-wine offering.
